title: One Hundred Years of Solitude
author: Gabriel García Márquez
summary: Seven generations of the Buendia family live and die in the isolated town of Macondo, where miracles, plagues, wars and repeating names blur together in a dreamlike chronicle of rise and fall.
readIf: you want a landmark of magical realism and don't mind a huge cast with similar names.
skipIf: you want a clear, linear plot or struggle to track a sprawling family tree.

pairings.reason: Another dazzling, myth-filled family chronicle that ties private lives to a nation's history.
Lyrical, nonlinear and family-centred, with a tighter focus and a heartbreak at its core.
A multi-generational family saga with a plainer style, which suits readers who want the sweep without the surrealism.
